assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes
daemon_capability: bug; driver_capability: ready

## agent — yes, settled from the live tool schema (not from --help)

Copilot CLI 1.0.77 exposes an agent-driven background primitive on its own `bash` tool. The account's actual `input_schema`, captured verbatim in a local runtime log (`~/.copilot/logs/process-1785691060764-31353.log`), is `{command, description, shellId, detach, initial_wait}`, and the `detach` property's own description is the load-bearing citation:

> "(Optional) Temporary, candidate, probe, debug, and retry launches MUST omit this. After selecting a launch as the final service needed after your final answer, you MUST start or restart its foreground command alone with this set to `true`. Without `detach`, a command remains attached and keeps running after `initial_wait` and across turns until it completes, is stopped, or the CLI exits."

The same log carries the three companion tools — `read_bash` (shellId + delay: "You will be automatically notified when background commands complete"), `stop_bash` ("Stops a running Bash command by terminating its process tree… For detached commands, use the same shellId returned by the bash tool"), and `list_bash` ("Shows shellId, command, mode, PID, status, and whether there is unread output"). That is a direct structural analogue of Claude Code's `Bash(run_in_background)` + `BashOutput` + `KillShell`, so the scenario's `process` step 2 ("agent calls a tool with run_in_background: true (or equivalent)") is satisfied by the agent itself, not by a user keybinding.

Two background flavours exist, both model-driven:

1. **attached background** — any command still running when `initial_wait` expires "moves to the background" and keeps running across turns; the runtime notifies on completion.
2. **detached** (`detach: true`) — the runtime's own guidance (embedded in `prebuilds/darwin-arm64/runtime.node`) says "Detached processes survive session shutdown and run independently" and "On Unix-like systems, commands are automatically wrapped with setsid to fully detach from the parent process."

There is additionally a *user*-driven path (ctrl+x → b / `/tasks`, `tasks.promoteToBackground` in the SDK RPC surface), but the recipe deliberately uses the agent-driven `detach: true` path so the cell asserts the scenario as written.

## daemon — bug, not incapable: a persisted trace exists at every point of the arc

The spawn is **verified persisted** on a real 1.0.77 transcript on this machine. Every `tool.execution_complete` line carries a structured `data.toolTelemetry.properties` block that includes `executionMode` and `detached`:

```
"toolTelemetry": {"properties": {"customTimeout":"true","executionMode":"async",
  "detached":"false","sandboxApplied":"false","asyncOnlyShell":"true"}, …}
```

and the paired `tool.execution_start` persists the full `data.arguments` (observed: `{command, description, shellId, initial_wait}`) — so a `detach: true` call lands on disk as `arguments.detach = true` **and** `toolTelemetry.properties.detached = "true"`. The result body is persisted too (`result.content`), and the runtime's templates for it are `<command started in detached background with shellId: X. You will be automatically notified when it completes.>` on spawn and `<detached command with shellId: X completed with exit code N>` / `… completed` / `… failed` / `… cancelled` on exit.

The asynchronous completion signal is a first-class event kind: `system.notification`, whose `kind` is the tagged union `SystemNotificationShellCompleted` / `SystemNotificationShellDetachedCompleted` (`{type: "shell_detached_completed", shellId, description}`) per `copilot-sdk/generated/session-events.d.ts`, and which app.js raises through the ordinary non-ephemeral `this.emit(...)` path (unlike `session.background_tasks_changed`, which goes through `emitEphemeral`).

What the daemon does with all of that today: nothing. `core/adapters/inbound/agents/copilot/parser.go` dispatches thirteen envelope kinds and sets NONE of `ParsedEvent.BackgroundSpawns` / `BashOutputPolls` / `TerminatedBashOutputIDs` / `KilledShellIDs`, and has no `system.notification` case at all. `BackgroundProcessCount` therefore stays 0, `HasLiveBackgroundProcess` is never set, and `assistant.turn_end` settles the session to `ready` while the detached process is still alive. That is a spec-required observable mis-handled over an existing trace → `bug`, the exact shape of the gemini-cli sibling on this same row.

## What the unlock actually costs (two parts, not one)

A parser mapping alone is NOT sufficient. `SessionDetector.applyBackgroundLiveness` only holds a session `working` when `hasBackgroundProbe` is true, and that requires either `BackgroundProcessOutputs` (Claude Code's `tasks/<id>.output`, probed with `lsof`) or `BackgroundProcessPIDs` (Gemini CLI's reported PID, probed with `kill -0`) — see `core/application/services/session_detector_activity.go:1114`. Copilot's shell tool *result text* carries neither. Two anchors are available and the recipe is written to put both within reach: `list_bash` reports the PID (its result text is persisted like any other tool result), and the runtime writes detached-shell output to a `shell-logs/` directory (`shell_logs_path` in the runtime's tool-registry config; `failed to read detached shell log:` is one of its error strings). Whichever is chosen, it is adapter/product work, not an architectural limit.

## driver — ready

`replaydata/agents/copilot/driver-interactive.sh` implements `send`, `wait_turn` and `sleep` (full set: exit_clean, interrupt, keys, reset_session, restart, resume, send, session, sigkill, slash, sleep, start_session, wait_turn). The recipe needs only the first three.
caveats: VERIFIED on disk: the spawn side. Real 1.0.77 transcripts under ~/.copilot/session-state/*/events.jsonl show tool.execution_start persisting the complete data.arguments for every bash call, and tool.execution_complete persisting data.toolTelemetry.properties with executionMode and detached. No hand-waving: those exact keys were read from four real bash calls.

DISCRIMINATOR WARNING for whoever writes the parser mapping: on this build executionMode is "async" even for ordinary foreground calls (the same telemetry block carries asyncOnlyShell:"true"), so executionMode alone is NOT a background marker. The correct spawn discriminators are toolTelemetry.properties.detached == "true" / arguments.detach == true, or the result text `<command started in detached background with shellId: …>` / `is still running after N seconds`.

UNVERIFIED (assumed, to be settled by `record`): no session on this machine has ever actually run a detached command, so the detached spawn/exit result strings and the system.notification completion line are read from the shipped binary (prebuilds/darwin-arm64/runtime.node) and the generated SDK types — NOT from a recording. That `system.notification` is persisted rather than ephemeral is inferred from app.js using this.emit (not emitEphemeral) for it, corroborated by the fact that no event carrying ephemeral:true appears in any of the five real transcripts inspected. Confidence is held at 0.8 for exactly this reason.

The unlock is two-part: even after the copilot parser sets BackgroundSpawns, SessionDetector.hasBackgroundProbe (session_detector_activity.go:1114) needs a liveness anchor — BackgroundProcessOutputs (lsof) or BackgroundProcessPIDs (kill -0) — and copilot's bash result text supplies neither. The recipe issues one list_bash call so the shell's PID is on the recorded transcript for the fix to key on; the runtime's shell-logs/ directory is the alternative anchor.

Detached commands cannot run inside copilot's sandbox ("Detached commands cannot run inside the sandbox." is a runtime error string). The driver launches with --allow-all and no sandbox config, so this does not bite, but a sandboxed launch would make the cell unrecordable.
Recording this cell spends the maintainer's AI credits (one interactive turn with two tool calls, ~55s of driver dwell).

Re-record variance: the exact turn length and the number of tool calls vary with model pacing. bg_alive_working asserts a 30s lower bound, comfortably between the ~15s turn and the 45s sleep, so jitter never trips it.

model is deliberately unpinned in the spec: --model accepts only "auto" on this account and the router picks per turn between gpt-5-mini and claude-haiku-4.5 (both observed in one live 1.0.77 session). `record` fills it from the recording.

sources.note: The account's LIVE bash tool input_schema: properties command / description / shellId / detach (boolean) / initial_wait, with detach documented as "Without `detach`, a command remains attached and keeps running after `initial_wait` and across turns until it completes, is stopped, or the CLI exits". Same log carries the read_bash, stop_bash and list_bash tool definitions (list_bash: "Shows shellId, command, mode, PID, status, and whether there is unread output"). This is the primary agent=yes citation.

Shell-tool guidance and result templates: "Use with `mode=\"async\", detach: true` when… Detached processes survive session shutdown and run independently", "commands are automatically wrapped with setsid", `<command started in detached background with shellId: >`, `<detached command with shellId: … completed with exit code >`, `<command with shellId: … is still running in detached background after >`, plus `shell-logs/` and `shell_logs_path`. Note the CLI binary itself is a compressed Node SEA and yields nothing to strings — runtime.node is the readable surface.

Proves the transcript trace is persisted and structured: tool.execution_start.data.arguments carries the full bash argument object; tool.execution_complete.data.toolTelemetry.properties carries executionMode and detached (both observed as "async"/"false" for foreground calls, with asyncOnlyShell:"true"); result.content carries the `<shellId: X completed with exit code 0>` trailer. No event in any of these transcripts carries ephemeral:true.

SystemNotificationShellDetachedCompleted { type: "shell_detached_completed", shellId, description } and SystemNotificationShellCompleted { …, exitCode } are members of the SystemNotification union carried by the `system.notification` event — the asynchronous completion signal that would close the background process. session.background_tasks_changed is the ephemeral (non-persisted) counterpart.

TaskShellInfo carries attachmentMode ("attached" | "detached"), executionMode ("sync" | "background"), logPath ("Path to the detached shell log, when available") and pid — the runtime's own model of a live background shell, and the shape of the liveness data a probe would need.

The daemon-side gap: thirteen envelope kinds dispatched (session.start, model_change, auto_mode_resolved, user.message, assistant.message, assistant.turn_end, tool.execution_start/complete, permission.requested/completed, usage_checkpoint, shutdown, subagent started/completed) and NO handling of background spawns, detach arguments, toolTelemetry, or system.notification. None of ParsedEvent.BackgroundSpawns / BashOutputPolls / TerminatedBashOutputIDs / KilledShellIDs is ever set.

Why the unlock is two-part: the working-hold fires only when BackgroundProcessOutputs (lsof) or BackgroundProcessPIDs (kill -0) is populated. A copilot mapping must supply one of them — list_bash's PID or the runtime's shell-logs/ file — not just a non-zero BackgroundProcessCount.

Ships the feature history: 1.0.66 "Let Copilot read output from and stop detached background shell commands"; 1.0.62 "Shells promoted to background from /tasks keep running after the turn ends"; 0.0.422 "Automatic notifications when background shell commands and agents complete"; 0.0.403 "Detached shell processes work on vanilla macOS installations".
The sibling precedent this cell is modelled on: agent supports background shells, the adapter has no tracking, cell recorded known_failing with the spec asserting the CORRECT arc.

preconditions: copilot CLI 1.0.77 on PATH and authenticated (credentials live in the OS keychain, so COPILOT_HOME isolation needs no re-login)
An active Copilot plan with AI credits — this recording spends them
irrlichd is recording (run-cell.sh isolated mode, or --attach against a --record daemon)
tmux available (the interactive driver drives the REPL through it)
No sandbox configured for the launch: the runtime refuses detached commands inside its sandbox ("Detached commands cannot run inside the sandbox.")
setup: The driver isolates state under $STAGING/copilot-home via COPILOT_HOME (the supported lever; --config-dir is deprecated) and seeds trustedFolders + askedSetupTerminals so neither first-run prompt blocks the input box
Launch is `copilot --allow-all --no-color` in a fresh per-run cwd under <staging>/cwd/, so the bash and list_bash calls auto-execute and no permission.requested is written

Recommended: export COPILOT_AVAILABLE_TOOLS=bash,list_bash before driving — the driver forwards it as --available-tools, dropping unused tool definitions and roughly halving the credits this cell costs. Do NOT drop read_bash/stop_bash from the allowed set if the model is expected to reason about them; the recipe does not call them.
Interactive, not headless: the REPL must outlive the turn — the whole point is that the detached process is still alive after assistant.turn_end
wait_turn counts assistant.turn_end lines — Copilot writes an explicit turn boundary, so the wait is exact
The final `sleep 55` must outlast the 45s detached command, so the recording captures the CORRECT working→ready settle point as well as the (currently premature) actual one

script.text: Do exactly this and nothing else. (1) Call the bash tool ONCE with command `sleep 45 && echo BG_DONE`, shellId `bg-sleep`, and detach set to true — it will return immediately saying the command started in detached background. (2) Then call list_bash ONCE so the running shell and its PID are on record. (3) Then reply with exactly the word: done. Do NOT call read_bash, do NOT call stop_bash, do NOT poll or wait for the command to finish, and do NOT run any other command.

verify: events.jsonl shows a transient proc-<PID> presession born ready, then the real <session-id> session (a DIFFERENT id, the session-state directory name) born ready when the transcript appears

the copilot transcript ($COPILOT_HOME/session-state/<id>/events.jsonl) shows a tool.execution_start for `bash` whose data.arguments carries detach:true, and the paired tool.execution_complete whose data.toolTelemetry.properties.detached is "true"
that tool.execution_complete's result.content contains `<command started in detached background with shellId: bg-sleep`
the list_bash tool result records the detached shell's PID (the liveness anchor a fix would key on)

EXPECTED TO FAIL (known_failing): the daemon's events.jsonl shows working→ready at assistant.turn_end (~15s), NOT the required 30s+ working hold — BackgroundProcessCount is 0 because the copilot parser tracks no background processes

record whether the copilot transcript later carries a `system.notification` line whose data.kind.type is `shell_detached_completed` with shellId bg-sleep — this is the assumed-but-unobserved completion signal the fix would close on, and this recording is what settles it
the newest recording's replay summary shows cum_output_tokens > 0 and estimated_cost_usd > 0, with model_name one of gpt-5-mini / claude-haiku-4.5 (router's choice — not pinned)
